Most Airmen work regular shifts on well-equipped bases, many with good housing, gyms and dining. Lots of jobs are technical, from aircraft maintenance to cyber. Deployments happen, but many jobs deploy less often or for shorter periods than ground forces.

Most Sailors go to an "A" School after boot camp to learn their rating (job). Advanced ratings, like the nuclear field, add more schools and long training pipelines. Some Sailors go straight to the fleet and learn on the job.

Most Soldiers live on large posts in the U.S., and some are stationed overseas in places like Germany, Korea and Japan. Days usually start with early-morning PT (physical training), then work in your job. Field exercises mean days or weeks living out of tents and vehicles. How often you deploy depends a lot on your unit and job.
Most members report to a unit first, learn on the job, and request "A" School later to learn their rating. Some go to "A" School right after boot camp.

The Air Force runs aircraft, airlift, refueling and a lot of the military's tech and cyber work. It's known for comfortable bases and many jobs that turn into civilian careers.

The Army handles land operations. Because it's so big, it has a huge range of jobs: infantry, armor, artillery, medicine, engineering, logistics, intelligence, cyber, and more helicopters than any other branch.

The Marine infantryman: patrols, raids and amphibious assaults.

The Marines deploy quickly by sea and air, often from Navy ships. It's part of the Department of the Navy. It's known for the toughest boot camp, strong tradition, and an "every Marine a rifleman" mindset, no matter the job.
The Marines don't have their own medics. Navy Hospital Corpsmen serve with Marine units, so the Navy is the way to be a Marine unit's medic.

The Military Entrance Processing Station (MEPS) is where you're checked out medically, pick your job and swear in. Every branch uses the same stations, spread across the country. Here's how the day usually goes.
The Naval Academy in Annapolis, Navy ROTC in college, or Officer Candidate School in Newport, Rhode Island.

The Naval Academy, Navy ROTC (Marine option), or Officer Candidates School in Quantico, Virginia. Every new Marine officer then spends about six months at The Basic School before training for their job.
The Navy operates on, under and above the sea worldwide. It has lots of technical jobs, from nuclear power and engineering to aviation, plus long deployments and port visits in other countries.
The Space Force doesn't have its own medical jobs. Air Force medical personnel take care of Guardians.

The Space Force has no separate Reserve or National Guard. A law passed in late 2023 lets it offer part-time service inside the Space Force itself, and it selected its first part-time Guardians (transferring from the Air Force Reserve) in 2026. Spots are limited, so ask a recruiter. The Air Force Reserve and Air National Guard are the closest part-time alternatives.
